items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S10642

SPONSOR: GONZALEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, the public service
law, the public authorities law, the energy law and the labor law, in
relation to enacting the responsible data center development act

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill establishes a one-year moratorium on the issuance of Depart-
ment of Environmental Conservation (DEC) permits for new data centers.
Thereafter, this bill requires a public hearing before issuance of a DEC
permit. The bill instructs the Department of Environmental Conservation
to complete an environmental impact report charting the current and
projected impacts on water, electricity, land use, tax revenue and
incentives, and pollution, and other adverse impacts of data center
operations in the state. The bill directs the PSC to create a separate
and distinct water and electric utility rate class for large data
centers to require that these facilities pay their full share of costs
to the grid and water infrastructure. The bill establishes renewable
energy and energy efficiency goals for data centers, as well as a commu-
nity benefits program that will fund community infrastructure and resi-
dential home upgrades for host communities of such facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: titles the bill the 'Responsible Data Center Development Act'

Section 2: establishes definitions, places a one-year moratorium on all
new data center-related DEC permits, requires a public hearing in the
host community before a data center can receive permitting approval, and
establishes the required contents of an environmental impact report DEC
is required to complete, including:

-Analysis of current data centers in the state and their land, water,
and electricity use and generation source;

-Projected growth of data centers in the state and their land, water,
and electricity use;

-Current and expected pollution (noise, water, air, GHG, e-waste) of
data centers;

-Impacts on disadvantaged communities and recognized indigenous nations;

An assessment of publicly-funded incentives received by data centers;
and

-5 Public comment periods in different regions of the state.

Section 3: Requires that the Public Service commission establish a new
electric rate class for data centers over 20MW, in which the data
centers are required to cover all additional costs of necessary infras-
tructure and administrative costs for connecting centers to the grid, in
addition to a community benefits program that provides localized support
and funding to communities hosting large data centers.

Section 4: Requires that the Public Service commission establish a new
water rate class for data centers over 20MW, in which the data centers
are required to cover all additional costs of necessary infrastructure
and administrative costs for water services and infrastructure servicing
large data centers.

Section 5: Bars any utility from being granted a rate increase without
the implementation of the new data center rate classes, which can occur
no later than June 1, 2030.

Section 6: Requires the formulation of an energy consumption efficiency
goal for data centers, inclusive of waste-heat recycling goals.

Section 7: Establishes energy efficiency goals for large data centers,
phasing in a 90% renewable energy by 2040 target for all data centers.
Data centers are also required to derive as much of it's energy needs as
technologically, environmentally, and practically feasible through
on-site renewable energy generation.

Section 8: Creates a host community benefits program for host communi-
ties where a large data center has been proposed to provide a variety of
infrastructure benefits to the community and mitigate deleterious
impacts.

Section 9: Requires the Long Island Power Authority to establish a
program for large data centers within its service territory that mirrors
the program required in section 8.

Section 10: Requires labor standards for construction of data centers
and includes prevailing wage, collective bargaining, apprenticeship
agreements, and "Buy American" requirements.

Section 11: Includes a severability clause.

Section 12: Sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Data Centers consume large amounts of energy and water. Their growing
proliferation across the state exacerbates the various issues caused by
such intensive resource consumption. These conditions put significant
pressure on local communities, infrastructure, utility rates, and the
environment. Other jurisdictions in the United States and in Europe have
responded by imposing regulatory controls on data center resource use.
This legislation aims to protect New York State residents from the nega-
tive impacts of large data centers and require that they equitably
distribute benefits to local host communities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

Minimal costs to the state. Local governments could experience benefits
from community infrastructure funding.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill is effective immediately.

summary: Places a one year moratorium on the issuance of data center permits; requires utilities to establish an independent classification of service for large data centers; sets energy efficiency goals for data centers; provides for benefits for host communities; sets labor standards for the construction of data centers.
title: Enacts the responsible data center development act
